newsitem.title: USA: Labor leader-Clinton "concerned" on welfare workers.
newsitem.headline: Labor leader-Clinton "concerned" on welfare workers.

text.p: AFL-CIO President John Sweeney met with President Clinton Friday and said Clinton wanted to make sure the nation's labour laws applied to those who must leave welfare to enter the workforce.

"The president expressed his concern and his desire to make sure that these people were considered as workers under the Fair Labour Standards Act and entitled to all protections under the law," Sweeney told reporters at the White House after meeting Clinton and other labour leaders.

The welfare reform law passed last year requires those on welfare to accept employment. But it is unclear how many of them will be covered by the Fair Labour Standards Act, which sets the minimum wage and requires overtime for work beyond 40 hours a week.
White House spokesman Mike McCurry said that the White House was looking at the law.
"We're weighing the application of the Fair Labour Standards Act to aspects of the welfare reform law," he told a reporter.
